children: Malaysian palm oil futures declined on Wednesday, weighed down by weakness in Chicago soyoil and crude oil prices, but stronger Dalian rivals capped losses.
The benchmark palm oil contract
for February delivery on the Bursa Malaysia Derivatives Exchange declined 19 ringgit, or 0.45%, to 4,221 ringgit ($1,026.26) a metric ton by 0242 GMT.
FUNDAMENTALS
Dalian's most-active soyoil contract (DBYcv1) rose 0.25, while its palm oil contract
added 1.28%. Soyoil prices on the Chicago Board of Trade
fell 0.39%.
Palm oil tracks the price movements of rival edible oils, as it competes for a share of the global vegetable oils market.
Crude oil prices fell on Wednesday, paring some of the previous day's gains, as concerns over supply disruptions in the Middle East were offset by rising supply and the prospect of a market surplus
Weaker crude oil prices make palm oil a less attractive option for biodiesel feedstock
Palm oil
may climb to 4,372 ringgit per metric ton, the peak of a wave b, Reuters technical analyst Wang Tao said.
MARKET NEWS
Asian stocks tumbled early on Wednesday as fresh US tariff threats hit sentiment and a tech-led rally fizzled, with the region's chip-heavy markets bearing the brunt of the selloff.
Ukraine has continued attacks on Russian oil refineries despite requests from US President Donald Trump to refrain, Russian leader Vladimir Putin said on Tuesday, pledging to retaliate.
